newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt share prices fall in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt share prices fall in brisk trade.

text.p: Egypt share prices on Sunday fell to their lowest level so far this month on the Cairo stock market in brisk trade swollen by the sale of state-owned shares in Egyptian American Bank.
The Capital Markets Authority (CMA) share index shed 1.86 points to close at 347.99 in trade worth 81.7 million pounds ($24 million).
The CMA said that 319,300 EAB shares were sold at 127 pounds per share, raising 40.5 million pounds. The Egyptian state Bank of Alexandria had offered 1.2 million shares.
Neveen al-Tahry of EAB Delta, one of the agents, said the offer was oversubscribed at a price of 110 to 112 pounds.
"However Bank of Alexandria stuck to their original price. They (the remaining shares) are being kept by Bank of Alexandria," she said.
EAB closed down 6.35 pounds at 120.65 pounds.
Another favourite bank, Commercial International Bank/CIB, fell 0.10 pounds to 72.5, when 3.0 million pounds worth of shares were traded.
The popular cement sector was relatively active, led by Amriyah Cement. The blue-chip firm had shares worth 7.5 million pounds changing hands. The share ended 2.0 pounds down at 82.
"Long-term investors are buying in Amriyah, but short-term investors are selling," said Elwi Taymour of EFG/Hermes.
Partially privatised Alexandria Flour Mills was the most active mill share. It closed down 2.98 at 80.
"Perhaps some investors are trying to buy bulk in the miller, particularly after the price fell below the offer price," said Taymour.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 475.18 points from 475.21 points on Thursday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 257.74 from 259.8 points.
Of the 87 shares traded, 27 rose, 32 fell while 28 ended unchanged, the CMA said.
